newsitem.title: ZIMBABWE: ZIMBABWE MONEY RATES EASIER IN LIQUID MARKET.
newsitem.headline: ZIMBABWE MONEY RATES EASIER IN LIQUID MARKET.

text.p: Short-term trading rates on Zimbabwe's money market were quoted largely easier on Tuesday, weighed down by continued excess liquidity.
"The market is very liquid. The Reserve Bank is selling short-term treasury bills on settlement which means that almost every day we are having lots of maturities," one dealer said.
NCDs redeemable after 30, 60 and 90 days were being bought at 20 percent versus Monday's 19.25 percent and selling at 18.5 percent compared to 19 percent.

The rates for bankers' acceptance bills were indicated at 19.5 percent and 18.5 percent (buying and selling respectively) versus 19.25 percent and 19 percent while treasury bills were selling at 18.25 percent compared to an 18.35-18.70 percent range overnight.
Call money was quoted slightly lower at 18 percent from 18.50 percent and figures from the Reserve Bank indicated a market surplus of Z$220.9 million.
